newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris court gives Moslem militants prison terms.
newsitem.headline: Paris court gives Moslem militants prison terms.

text.p: A Paris court on Thursday passed jail sentences of up to eight years on members of an alleged militant Moslem support network accused of ordering attacks in Morocco including one in which two Spaniards died in 1994.

Abdelilah Ziyad, a Moroccan aged 38 who admitted setting up the network to undermine King Hassan II, was given an eight-year sentence. A second alleged ringleader who is on the run, Mohamed Zinedine, 36, was sentenced in his absence to eight years in jail.
Djamel Lounici, an Algerian fundamentalist aged 34 currently detained in Italy, was sentenced in his absence to five years.
Prosecutors had requested jail terms of up to 10 years for the accused.
Police said the network was dismantled after four guerrilla attacks in Moroccu in 1994 including the shooting of the Spanish tourists during a robbery at a Marrakesh hotel.
The trial opened in December days after a rush-hour bomb attack on a Paris commuter train killed four people, spurring fears of revenge attacks on France by fundamentalist guerrillas.
